text:
Anonymous post for another group member
Ive lived here several years already and haven't learned enough Hebrew. Looking for self-learning discipline tips, encouragement and hoping someone can relate.

I can read, have a few hundred words, and understand more than I speak, but I always ask people to speak English. When people find out how long Ive been here, responses range from confused to offended. And I get it.

I try not to flinch away from any lectures, but I don't need to be convinced that I should learn/should have been fluent a long time ago. I understand all the reasons very well and am very embarrassed of myself. I don't have any excuse or reason-- its not "I don't want to" and I don't think it's too hard; it's a failure of discipline on my part that I take full responsibility for. It's easy enough to get by where I live with English and basic Hebrew reading. So, it happened more easily than people may think. But I'm not proud of it.

Recently I have been putting more effort in, but I won't be able to have my next interview in Hebrew. My partner is very disappointed and whenever we near an interview, it becomes a big point of tension. He believes it hurts my case.

And of course, he and everyone we know speaks several languages. So no one really pities me 😅 and I just feel... pretty lame 🥲

I want to be better, but I've gotten to a point that feeling bad about myself is impeding my efforts as well. So, I'm just hoping I'm not the only one who's been in this position so far into the process.
